compatibility_audit.deployment: DepthExtractor loaders in the sibling DeepDesktop deployment checkouts
evidence: Depth Anything V2 loaders construct Python modules and load .pth state dicts with weights_only=True.
The deployed loader sources contain no torch.jit.load or vulkan_prepack references.
No .pt, .pth, .ts, .jit, or .torchscript artifacts are checked into the deployed loader/template roots outside their vendored PyTorch checkout.
TensorRT .ts cache names are produced and consumed only by TensorRT loader variants and do not establish Vulkan schema compatibility.
compatibility_audit.recheck_when: a deployment starts loading serialized TorchScript, ExportedProgram, or custom-class artifacts
compatibility_audit.scope: fork-owned Vulkan operator schemas and custom classes

ledger_entries.summary: Graph correctness execution, generic eager kernels and contexts, retained packed-weight caches, public Vulkan Python APIs, and evidence-critical diagnostics including generic sync, submit, and retire attribution.
VisionBlocks model orchestration and the stack proof/canary control plane remaining in Sync and Context after generic counter extraction.
Replay bundles, compiled sessions, their public bridges, and stale-output diagnostics.
Eager inference-graph, scratch-arena, readback, execution-program, and runtime-policy surfaces. Retained packed-weight and linear-context caches are isolated in PackedWeightCache.*.

Allocation-label model-lane inference and device-name policy checks. VulkanGraphPlanningContext now carries explicit request fields through graph lowering and execution; eager label/tensor inference and device-name heuristics remain isolated in LegacyPlanningInference.* and LegacyDeviceNamePolicy.h.

basis: Qwen is not in the five-model Vulkan coverage corpus.
The deployed Qwen loader targets Qwen 2.5 through transformers and has no Vulkan custom-op callsite.
Repository reachability outside tests ends inside the Qwen/gated-delta implementation, registration, and legacy planning caches.
scope_decisions.consequence: The Qwen linear-attention context, gated-delta operators and shader, mechanism tests, dedicated GatedDeltaSplit planning cache, and residual Qwen/gated-delta label sentinels were deleted. Generic planning-label inference remains Migration in LegacyPlanningInference.* until its separate explicit-field and lane-parity gate is met.

basis: The fused-head admission predicate returned false unconditionally because the shader was not numerically aligned with the reference DPT head across supported decoder shapes.
The supported plain eager route already executes the decoder tail as concrete conv, bilinear upsample, conv, ReLU, conv, and ReLU operations.
No VulkanGraphProgram lowering consumes the shader; the broader replay and compiled-session machinery remains fail-closed and Migration-gated.
scope_decisions.consequence: The inactive shader, exact DAv2 constants, admission checks, output preparation, dispatch branch, and fused-route log label were deleted. The composed decoder tail and its DAv2 behavioral coverage remain; replay and compiled-session deletion gates are unchanged.

basis: The opt-in canary removed one selected phase-boundary submit and intermittently corrupted private-capture output.

Its behavior-changing branch had already been backed out; the direct hook returned false, and its remaining authorization input only selected a different fail-closed diagnostic for the retained single-recording canary.
Generic boundary, barrier, submit-ordering, and single-recording proof surfaces remain available for the graph-owned region replacement.
scope_decisions.consequence: The inactive environment route, submit-hook observer, graph rows, live-submit exact-join schema, collector plumbing, and mechanism-only test were deleted. Current-topology submits remain preserved, and behavioral tests continue to cover repeated output parity and fail-closed single-recording ownership.

basis: The canary was default-off and reachable only through explicit environment orchestration.
Its DAv2 result proved that 48 plain-linear flushes could be deferred with bit-for-bit output parity, but did not establish a supported eager default or a graph-owned replacement.
Supported eager linear retains its explicit pending-command flush and submit-origin accounting while graph programs pursue packed-context ownership directly.
scope_decisions.consequence: The canary context-retention owner, eager branch, environment registration, evidence-harness exemption, and mechanism test were deleted. The supported default linear flush and its submit-origin regression test remain.

basis: The lazy-chain, deferred-region, runtime shader compile, and command-list surfaces were default-off behavior-neutral observers over eager op-hit backlogs.
Their own plans recorded execution_enabled=0 because they lacked tensor SSA handles, producer-consumer edges, output ownership, descriptor capture, barrier execution, and alias proof.

Graph lowering and VulkanGraphProgram now own semantic regions and command partitions directly, so retaining a second backlog-based planning model would preserve the rejected architecture rather than reusable execution code.
scope_decisions.consequence: The eager backlog observer state, flush-boundary hooks, behavior-neutral runtime compiler and command-list planners, provenance-only deferred handles, mechanism tests, and stack-era documentation were deleted. Failure logging, fallback/readback counters, submit-origin accounting, transition diagnostics, and GPU timestamp attribution remain active.

basis: Repository reachability for runtime glslc compilation, owned SPIR-V descriptors, live eager-chain recording, and deferred tensor placeholders ended in the experiment implementations, private schemas, mechanism tests, and four VisionBlocks call sites.
No graph lowering or VulkanGraphProgram consumer used the shader-expression generator or owned-SPIR-V path.

Standalone fp32 buffer add/mul shader parity succeeded, but DAv2 stack bridge sanity repeatedly failed across runtime-generated and static shaders, copied input leases, and explicit materialization boundaries, rejecting eager tensor handles as value-lifetime or output-ownership proof.
scope_decisions.consequence: The runtime compiler, owned-SPIR-V support, live sidecar, placeholder registry and consumer hooks, generated VisionBlocks routes, private schemas, environment gates, and mechanism tests were deleted. Concrete eager kernels and token-prefix buffer writes remain supported. The generic graph-scope deferred-registration guard survives with a direct C++ behavioral regression test.

basis: Production VisionBlocks only implements the native private-device-baton mode; the Python-mediated spelling was benchmark-local orchestration.
The Python-mediated canary overflowed the Windows stack inside run_vision_backbone_stack_private_capture_debug and never established a supported route.
The checked-in performance evidence manifest preserves the rejection result, so the live benchmark only needs a generic unsupported-mode fail-closed path.
scope_decisions.consequence: Dedicated unsafe-mode constants, planning fields, and status branches were deleted. The historical python_private_baton spelling now follows the generic unsupported-mode path, and a behavioral regression test still proves it cannot authorize deep-stack execution.

basis: The per-stack command/descriptor pool lease was default-off and reachable only through explicit environment orchestration.
Focused DAv2 vits_140 evidence was correctness-clean but slower than the supported persistent-pool default and did not fix the compiled-session stack overflow it targeted.
The accepted stack-planned descriptor-pool lease is a separate default lifetime fix and remains unchanged.
scope_decisions.consequence: The environment branch, per-stack command/descriptor pools, timeline-retirement callback, cancellation path, and mechanism-only retained-state field were deleted. Stack-owned external recording continues to use the supported persistent pools, their global-completion reset diagnostics remain, and the accepted stack-planned descriptor-pool lease is preserved.

basis: The fixed-width-six route was a default-off exact environment spelling over the shared segmented stack-owned recording planner.

Focused DAv2 vits_140 evidence was correctness-clean and reduced stack-planned submits relative to the retained wide4 canary, but was slower and left retire-drain pressure unchanged; no supported default depends on the exact wide6 route.
The wide4 canary remains the current retained bounded lane, while the checked-in evidence manifest and canary decision table preserve the wide6 result and rejection reason.
scope_decisions.consequence: The accepted environment spelling, width-six constants and plan wrapper, selection branch, benchmark allowlist entry, and mechanism-only test were deleted. The generic fixed-width planner, retained wide4 specialization, stack recording diagnostics, and historical wide6 measurements remain.

basis: Wide3 and the prefix3-6 tail variants were default-off exact environment spellings over shared fixed-width and dispatch-budget segment planners.
The recorded DAv2 vits_140 RX 9070 sweep kept all five routes correctness-clean with zero fallback/readback, but every route was slower than the retained wide4 canary.

No supported default or VulkanGraphProgram caller selects these exact modes; the evidence manifest preserves each timing row and the shared planners remain exercised by retained wide4 and prefix3 routes.
scope_decisions.consequence: The five accepted spellings, wide3 constants and plan wrapper, prefix-tail scope ladder and tail-to-exit execution branch, benchmark allowlist entries, and mechanism-only tests were deleted. The generic fixed-width and dispatch-budget planners, prefix3 and wide4 modes, context-owned remainder recording, stack diagnostics, and historical measurements remain.

basis: The exact stack_internal_until_stack_exit spelling was a default-off diagnostic override with no supported caller, benchmark entry, or focused mechanism test.
It only allowed a smaller stack-exit retire-source snapshot to supersede the preserved phase-submit source; it did not transfer resources, defer submits, or authorize submit elision.

The selected synthetic residual2-to-norm1 boundary still reported a partial source and failed closed on pending_retire_transfer_source_incomplete, while the preserved-phase handoff remains the live migration route.
scope_decisions.consequence: The exact environment spelling, selector helper, source-overwrite branch, work-batch state, and mode-specific diagnostic field were deleted. Generic control-plane work-batch rows, pending-retire source snapshots and coverage diagnostics, and preserved_phase_submit_handoff behavior remain.

basis: The label-inferred broad tiled-linear route failed full DAv2 bridge parity, and the narrower exact FC2 route was correctness-clean but substantially slower than the retained supported lane.
Later exact FC2 vec2 and QKV tiled contracts also failed full bridge isolation despite passing local operator tests, so the conservative buffer-linear route remains the supported default.
The generic tiled kernels remain available for contract-backed plans; only the retired environment selector and its exact-route helpers are forbidden.
scope_decisions.consequence: The environment read, exact FC2/vec2 selection helpers, benchmark orchestration, and mechanism-only route tests were deleted. Generic tiled kernels remain, while behavioral fail-closed tests continue to pin the full-bridge correctness bug class.

basis: The legacy QKV-only environment spelling duplicated the already-proven stack-internal retire-batch predicate without naming the reusable ownership contract.
PYTORCH_VULKAN_STACK_SCOPE_RETIRE_HANDOFF is the contract-facing replacement and covers QKV plus later proven stack-scoped activation and LayerNorm statistic-buffer classes.
No supported caller or compatibility artifact depends on the private legacy spelling.
scope_decisions.consequence: The legacy environment alias, selector helper, and alias-only mechanism test were deleted. StackScopeRetireHandoffContract and its evidence-critical diagnostics remain the sole live path.

basis: The canary safely moved exact external-recording cleanup entries to the existing stack-exit timeline, but did not reduce the measured stack-owner retire-drain submit count.
The RX 9070 DAv2 vits_140 probe regressed device-resident mean latency from about 64.3 ms to 75.3 ms.
A future handoff requires segment-local completion ownership or a separate submit-plan change, not restoration of the same stack-exit transfer.
scope_decisions.consequence: The environment selector, transfer helper and movement branch, and mechanism-only test were deleted. Generic external-recording cleanup rows remain metadata-only and continue to prove that no pending retires move.

basis: The poll-only deferral canary reduced retire-poll accounting but left the stack-owner retire-queue submit count unchanged.
The RX 9070 DAv2 vits_140 probe remained correctness-clean but regressed device-resident mean latency from about 64.3 ms to 67.0 ms.
The accepted narrow stack-owned segment retire-drain deferral uses explicit resource-count and byte budgets and remains the supported policy.
scope_decisions.consequence: The poll-only environment read, selector helper, and early-return branch were deleted. The accepted bounded stack-owned segment retire-drain deferral and generic retire counters remain.

basis: The attention no-clone JSON hook had no supported harness or test caller and duplicated the selected SDPA branch solely to compare direct and materialized results through synchronous CPU readback.
Behavioral transition and op-hit tests now pin direct-safe attention probability parity, zero fallback, zero buffer copies, and fail-closed materialization-required rows without the one-off logger.
The vision-owner text log had no supported caller and duplicated owner selection data retained in the evidence-harness vision owner counters plus generic route and runtime-policy diagnostics.
scope_decisions.consequence: The two environment reads, dedicated file writers, duplicate SDPA execution/readback branch, and call-site bookkeeping were deleted. Vision owner counters, generic route/runtime-policy logs, transition logs, op-hit evidence, and behavioral no-clone tests remain.

basis: The opt-in selector had no supported caller and only wrapped the post-stack LayerNorm and decoder-preprocess island in the benchmark-only stack bridge lane.
Its historical RX 9070 DAv2 vits_140 measurement was correctness-clean at about 77.7 ms median, but opt-in stack lanes are historical evidence rather than supported deletion bars.
Exact-SHA 25b66ba0b8b supported VulkanGraphProgram evidence owns complete DAv2 execution and establishes graph-owned command partitions as the replacement for fixed bridge submission cost.
scope_decisions.consequence: The environment read, bridge recording scope, and mechanism-only scope-closed diagnostic field were deleted. Historical JSON manifests retain the measured configuration and result. Behavioral graph rows and tests continue to prove decoder consumption completes before bridge exit without public/host/readback escape.

basis: The benchmark mode allowlist contains only stack_capture_decoder_preprocess, and constructor validation rejected compiled_session_bridge before any compiled-session state could be reached.
The remaining backend-name selector and compiled-session call branch were therefore unreachable code, not a live Migration caller.
The replay and compiled-session backend stays Migration until graph-owned recorded partitions satisfy its separate lifetime and stale-output gate.
scope_decisions.consequence: The unreachable benchmark constant set, special quarantine branch, backend-name selector, and compiled-session invocation branch were deleted. Generic unsupported-mode handling still rejects the historical spelling in a behavioral regression; public replay/compiled-session APIs remain Migration rather than being expanded or prematurely removed.

basis: The three predicates were introduced with the original model-lane policy but never gained a tracked production, benchmark, or test caller.
Current route selection consumes infer_model_lane plus contract and route-policy decisions directly; no supported eager or graph path consults these predicates.
Their compiled-replay and generic-SDPA booleans encode superseded global lane permissions rather than the current fail-closed contract and graph-program direction.
scope_decisions.consequence: The unused declarations and definitions were deleted. Live infer_model_lane/model_lane_name behavior and the still-open legacy label-inference Migration gate are unchanged.

basis: The removed execution-object, execution-program, tensor-slot, and wrapper-replay accessors had declarations and definitions but no tracked production, benchmark, or test caller.
No removed method was registered as an operator schema or custom class method, and the deployment compatibility audit found no serialized Vulkan planning API consumer.
Live cache keys, storage construction, allocation metadata, program slots, replay phase steps, resident-byte accounting, and evidence-critical generic diagnostics remain unchanged.
scope_decisions.consequence: Unused introspection and view-construction APIs, their dead metadata storage, and mechanism-only log fields were deleted without changing live planning, cache, replay, or allocation behavior. The owning subsystems remain Migration until their graph replacement gates close.

basis: KV sequence length was assigned on attention-program creation, cache hits, and replay lookup but had no remaining read after the unused cache-view API was deleted.

The sequence values were absent from cache and replay keys, and every live call supplied the current key/value tensor extent against an identically sized storage spec, making the capacity check tautological.

The reset and sequence-update diagnostic fields had no benchmark, test, evidence-manifest, or production-log consumer; KV allocation hits, stores, identity, storage ownership, and resident-byte accounting remain live.
scope_decisions.consequence: Write-only sequence state, propagation parameters, tautological validation, and mechanism-only counters were deleted. The separate storage allocation was audited independently and is retired by unused_kv_cache_planning_storage.

basis: The separate KV cache object allocated tensors and charged them to attention-program residency, but no eager kernel, replay command, graph binding, or KV append contract ever populated or read those tensors.

The KV planning descriptor affected only the unused allocation, a positional query_runtime_policy diagnostic slice, and program/cache keys for that allocation; it did not select a kernel or bind actual key/value state.

create_kv_cache_storage_for_request had one mechanism-only test caller and no production, benchmark, Python entry-point, or serialized consumer. Compatibility is empty, while real eager KV tensors and graph output-to-input state replay remain unchanged.
scope_decisions.consequence: The unused KV planning descriptor, unbound storage cache, public test hook, diagnostic tuple fields, and mechanism-only tests were deleted. Active KV append kernels and generated graph state replay are separate surfaces and remain covered.

basis: ScratchArena defined/execution-layout/persistent, ReadbackBufferObject defined/persistent, and attention/decoder program persistent accessors had definitions but no production, benchmark, test, or evidence caller.
Scratch storage, size, alignment, reset, reserve, identity, cache keys, and retire provenance remain live; readback buffer, size, mutex, identity, and hit/store diagnostics remain live in Copy.
VisionBackboneProgram persistence is intentionally retained because the stack resource-binding evidence harness emits it as stable program-slot ownership evidence.
scope_decisions.consequence: Caller-free accessors, duplicate stored metadata, and the resulting one-field readback spec wrapper were deleted. Live scratch allocation, generic readback caching, evidence diagnostics, and vision program persistence are unchanged.

basis: create_scratch_arena_storage_for_request had one mechanism-only test caller and no production, benchmark, Python entry-point, or serialized consumer.

The public hook merely reconstructed the same scratch policy and returned its backing tensor; real attention, norm, linear, and vision callers use prime_labeled_scratch_arena_for_request or program-owned arenas directly.
Behavioral execution-object tests continue to require scratch store, hit, reset, reserve, and byte-accounting events through real kernels.
scope_decisions.consequence: The operator schema, CPU/Vulkan registrations, raw-storage constructor bridge, and mechanism-only assertion were deleted; internal scratch planning and behavioral coverage remain live.

basis: The const scratch-arena, replay-program, decoder skip, and decoder-head program overloads had declarations and definitions but no production, benchmark, test, or evidence caller.
Attention-runtime and decoder-head replay-step adapters likewise had no caller; backbone and decoder replay-step adapters remain live in stack execution.
Mutable program, scratch, slot, and decoder-head accessors remain heavily used by eager and replay execution, and no replay state, command recording, submission, or lifetime behavior changed.
scope_decisions.consequence: Zero-caller overloads and step adapters were deleted. The live mutable execution surface plus used backbone/decoder replay steps remain Migration under their existing graph-replacement gates.

basis: query_runtime_policy had two test callers and no production, benchmark, Python entry-point, or serialized consumer; it returned a positional encoding of internal policy fields without executing the selected route.

The LLM decode scheduler regression now runs a corpus-backed HY-MT buffer-backed SDPA shape under an explicit planning scope, verifies numerical parity, and checks the emitted split boundary, attention family, execution strategy, scratch, and ownership fields.

The minimum capability regression now runs real Vulkan MM, verifies numerical parity, and checks capability/runtime logs reject cooperative-matrix selection. Runtime policy and capability logs remain evidence-critical diagnostics.
scope_decisions.consequence: The public schema, CPU/Vulkan registrations, positional policy encoder, and mechanism-only assertions were deleted. Stronger real-operation behavioral regressions preserve decode routing and capability masking.

basis: The six individual reset schemas had no production, benchmark, test, Python entry-point, or deployed-artifact caller. Two stale documentation examples were their only non-registration references.

The supported reset_fallback_counters schema remains widely used and already invokes every underlying reset function in the same process, preserving buffer-copy, clone, pointwise-conv, retire-call-site, submit-origin-phase, and stack-scratch evidence isolation.
All snapshot and counter query schemas remain live. Only redundant public reset registrations were removed; the underlying C++ reset functions remain available to the aggregate reset path.
A behavioral regression now verifies the aggregate reset clears every affected query surface without depending on any deleted per-surface reset mechanism.
scope_decisions.consequence: Six redundant reset schemas and registrations were deleted. The aggregate reset, underlying reset implementations, evidence queries, benchmark snapshots, and behavioral diagnostics remain unchanged.

basis: attention_subgroup_capabilities had no production, benchmark, test, Python entry-point, documentation, or deployed-artifact caller.

The internal attention_subgroup_capabilities_snapshot function remains live in vision stack policy and was not changed; capability-profile tests continue to exercise route behavior through real Vulkan operations.
Generic runtime-policy, attention-plan, device-property, and capability-profile diagnostics remain the supported evidence surfaces.
scope_decisions.consequence: The zero-caller public capability schema and registration were deleted while the live internal capability decision and behavioral tests remain.

basis: Four Context helpers for stack-stat snapshots, immediate descriptor-lease release, stack-internal batch clearing, and full fence-wait flush had declarations and definitions but no production, benchmark, test, callback, or function-pointer caller.

The bridge-private capture pending-retire batch stored mutexes and resource vectors plus clear, restore, timeline-retire, and retained-state reporting code, but no producer ever inserted or moved a resource into the batch; all reported counts were structurally zero.

Live stack-region pending-retire handoff, timeline-gated descriptor-pool lease retirement, retire_after_fence_wait descriptor policy, returned end/cancel recording statistics, and bridge-private release-owner proof rows remain unchanged.
scope_decisions.consequence: The permanently empty bridge-private pending-retire scaffold, its always-zero retained-state fields, and four zero-caller Context wrappers were deleted. Live cleanup ownership and evidence-critical bridge proof diagnostics remain.

basis: Repository reachability for the vTensor CPU-size, padded-size, and extent UBO accessors ends at their declarations and definitions; no production, test, benchmark, callback, function-pointer, or dispatcher caller exists.

Every constructor initialized the three shared pointers to null, so their alias checks, graph-resource release branches, and resize updates were structurally inactive in all supported eager and VulkanGraphProgram executions.
The live metadata_uniform_ and buffer_metadata path remain unchanged and continue to carry logical sizes, strides, buffer length, and storage offset for direct-buffer shaders.
scope_decisions.consequence: Three permanently null shared pointers were removed from every vTensor together with their unreachable lazy allocation, alias-validation, resource-release, and resize machinery. Live buffer metadata and graph-owned scratch retirement remain unchanged.

basis: The manual MemoryAllocator allocation factory, staging-buffer factory, resource requirement queries, bind helpers, and vTensor facade had declarations and definitions but no production, test, benchmark, callback, or function-pointer caller.

Every live image, storage buffer, uniform buffer, tensor storage, readback object, and graph scratch allocation already requested immediate VMA-backed allocation; allocate_memory=false existed only as an unselected parameter chain.

The vTensor reallocate and virtual_resize entry points, their metadata updater, and the storage discard/reallocate implementation likewise had no caller; Vulkan does not register aten::resize_ and graph programs create shape-specific storage instead.

Live has_memory and owns_memory evidence, allocation identities and generations, failure snapshots, residency accounting, host-visible buffer policy, and timeline retirement remain on the immediate VMA path.
scope_decisions.consequence: The unselected deferred/manual allocation route, unused staging helper, and caller-free tensor resizing machinery were deleted. Vulkan resources now store their VMA allocation handle directly; supported allocation behavior and evidence-critical ownership, failure, residency, and retirement diagnostics are unchanged.
